1.title: Chapter 1: The First Night
1.summary: The outbreak begins. You wake to screaming and have minutes to decide who lives, who dies, and who you become.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: 3:47 AM. The screaming woke you.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Not the neighbors fighting again. Something worse. Something that doesn't sound human.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Your phone buzzes. A message from Marcus: 'Don't open the door. Don't go outside. They're everywhere.'

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Someone is banging on your apartment door. The sound is desperate. Human. You think.

dialogue.speaker: unknown
dialogue.text: Please! Please open the door! They're coming! I can hear them on the stairs!

choices.text: Open the door — let them in
Stay quiet — don't answer
Look through the peephole first

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You throw the lock. The door flies open and a woman crashes into your arms, shaking.

dialogue.speaker: elena
dialogue.text: Thank god. Thank you. I thought... I saw them take Henderson down the hall. They just... they bit into him and he...

dialogue.speaker: elena
dialogue.text: We need to leave. The building. They're working through floor by floor.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You press your back against the wall and hold your breath.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The banging stops. Then a sound you'll never forget — wet, tearing, and the voice that was begging goes silent.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Minutes pass. Something drags itself away from your door. You're alone.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You press your eye to the peephole. A woman in her thirties, pajamas, barefoot. Behind her, something is crawling on the ceiling of the hallway.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: It has Henderson's face. But its joints bend the wrong way. And it's smiling.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The woman hasn't seen it yet. It's three meters behind her. You have seconds.

choices.text: Yell through the door — 'GET DOWN!'
Throw the door open and pull her inside
Watch. Say nothing.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The thing on the ceiling lunges. Elena throws herself through your doorway as you slam the door shut.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Something hits the other side. Once. Twice. Then it moves on.

dialogue.speaker: elena
dialogue.text: What... what WAS that? That was Henderson. I've lived next to him for two years. That was Henderson.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Your apartment is on the 7th floor. The fire escape leads to the alley. The elevator is a death trap. The stairs... you heard something on them.

dialogue.speaker: marcus_text
dialogue.text: [Marcus]: I'm on the 4th floor. I have a car in the garage. Get to me and we go. NOW.

choices.text: Take the fire escape down
Risk the stairwell to reach Marcus
Barricade here and wait for sunrise

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The fire escape groans under your weight. Seven floors of rusted metal and the sounds of the city tearing itself apart below.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Halfway down, you see a supply bag on the 4th floor landing. Marcus's floor.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The stairwell is dark. Emergency lights flicker. On the 6th floor landing, blood drags in a long smear down the stairs.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You hear something breathing on the 5th floor. It's not human breathing.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You push the couch against the door. Wedge a chair under the knob. It won't hold forever, but maybe until morning.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Hours pass. The sounds outside get worse. Then, silence. The worst kind.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: At dawn, you hear a voice in the hallway. Marcus. He sounds wrong. 'Let me in,' he says. 'I made it. Open up.'

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Marcus's voice. But you've known Marcus for five years. That cadence is off. He's speaking too slowly. Too carefully. Like he's reading lines.

dialogue.speaker: marcus
dialogue.text: Come on, open the door. It's me. I'm fine. I'm totally fine. I just need to come in. Please.

choices.text: Open the door for Marcus
Tell Marcus to slide his ID under the door
Stay silent. Don't respond.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You move the couch. The door swings open. Marcus is standing there, smiling. His eyes are milk-white. The bite mark on his neck is still bleeding.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: He lunges.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You ask him to slide his ID under the door. There's a long pause.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Then the sound of something heavy hitting the wall. A guttural, inhuman shriek. And then running. Down the stairs. Away.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: That wasn't Marcus.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You say nothing. The voice outside repeats itself. Slower. Then it makes a sound — not a word. Something between a growl and a laugh.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: It leaves. You hear it descend the stairwell, each step heavier than the last.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Dawn breaks gray and ugly over the city. From your window, you can see fires. Cars abandoned in the street. Figures moving wrong in the distance.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Marcus's last message, from hours ago: 'If you get this, I'm already gone. The keys to the truck are under the visor. Get out of the city. Don't stop.'

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You make it to the parking garage. Marcus's truck is there. Keys under the visor, just like he said.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: But someone is already at the truck. A teenager, maybe sixteen. Blood on his shirt. A bite on his arm, fresh. He sees you.

dialogue.speaker: teenager
dialogue.text: Please. I stole this from a dead guy. I didn't know whose it was. Take it. I don't care. Just — can I come with you? I can't stay here.

choices.text: Take the kid with you
Take the truck, leave the kid
Ask about the bite before deciding

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You ask about the bite. He looks at it like he forgot it was there.

dialogue.speaker: danny
dialogue.text: It's... I don't know. My dog bit me? It was my dog. He went crazy this morning and I—

dialogue.speaker: danny
dialogue.text: It doesn't matter. Please. I can help. I know how to drive. I know the city. Don't leave me here.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The bite looks wrong. The skin around it is turning gray. You've seen enough horror movies. But he's a kid.

choices.text: Take him. You can figure it out later.
Tie off the wound and take him — but watch him
Tell him the truth — you can't risk it

dialogue.speaker: danny
dialogue.text: Thank you. I swear I won't be a problem. I know the back roads out of the city. My dad taught me before he...

dialogue.speaker: danny
dialogue.text: There's a gas station on Route 9. We can stock up there.

dialogue.speaker: danny
dialogue.text: Yeah. Yeah, I get it. I'd leave me too.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You get in the truck. In the mirror, the kid sits on the curb. He doesn't move. He doesn't watch you go.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You don't know how long a bite takes. You don't know if you just killed him or saved yourself.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The city burns behind you. The highway is empty. Whatever you did tonight — who you saved, who you left, who you let in — it's with you now.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The dead don't forget. And neither does the kid in your backseat. If he's there.

2.title: Chapter 2: The Gas Station
2.summary: Route 9. The first stop. Supplies are low and trust is tested. What you do here determines who's still alive at the end.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Route 9. The gas station sits alone in a sea of dead grass. The lights are on. That should be reassuring. It isn't.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: There's a group inside. You can see them through the windows. Four, maybe five people. They have guns.

dialogue.speaker: garcia
dialogue.text: Slow and easy. Hands where I can see them. I've shot three people this week who moved too fast.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: A man steps out the front door. Shotgun, low and ready. Not pointed at you. Not pointed away either.

dialogue.speaker: garcia
dialogue.text: That's far enough. How many in the vehicle? Any bites?

dialogue.speaker: priya
dialogue.text: He will use it, if he has to. Don't give him a reason.

choices.text: Tell the truth about your group
Lie — say it's just you, no bites
Wait for nightfall, sneak in for supplies

dialogue.speaker: garcia
dialogue.text: Honest. I respect that. Most people lie.

dialogue.speaker: garcia
dialogue.text: I used to run a checkpoint outside São Paulo. Two hundred people a day lied to my face. You know what honesty is worth now? Everything.

dialogue.speaker: garcia
dialogue.text: The kid with the bite stays outside. I don't care if it's a dog bite or a zombie bite. Outside. That's the deal.

dialogue.speaker: priya
dialogue.text: He's right. The kid stays outside the fence. But I'll leave him a blanket. It gets cold.

dialogue.speaker: garcia
dialogue.text: Just you. Alright. Come in. But I'm watching.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Garcia's eyes linger on Danny a beat too long. He might know. Or he might just be careful. Either way, you're inside.

dialogue.speaker: priya
dialogue.text: Nobody travels alone anymore. Nobody. Remember that when you tell us your story later.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You wait. Hours. The sun drops. The group inside settles into watches. The back door has a padlock you can pick.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You slip in through the back. Aisle three. The shelves are still half-stocked.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: A flashlight hits your face. A woman, rifle aimed at your chest.

dialogue.speaker: priya
dialogue.text: Don't move. Don't even breathe wrong. Garcia! We've got a thief.

dialogue.speaker: priya
dialogue.text: I had a sister who trusted the wrong stranger. I buried what was left of her myself. So no — I don't give warnings twice.

choices.text: Drop to your knees and surrender
Grab what you can and run

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You shove the shelf. Bottles crash. You sprint for the back door with a bag of supplies.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: A shot rings out. Glass shatters above your head. You make it to the truck. Danny is screaming. You drive.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: They'll remember you. And you just made enemies on a road with nowhere to hide.

dialogue.speaker: garcia
dialogue.text: We've been here three days. Military radio went dead yesterday. Last transmission said there's a safe zone — Riverside, forty miles north.

dialogue.speaker: garcia
dialogue.text: I had fourteen people under my command before all this. Nine made it to this gas station. Four since. Do the math on my patience.

dialogue.speaker: garcia
dialogue.text: We're heading there at dawn. You're welcome to come. But I need to know — and I need the truth — what happened to your friend Marcus?

dialogue.speaker: garcia
dialogue.text: So I'll ask once. What happened to Marcus?

choices.text: Tell Garcia everything about Marcus
Give a vague answer — 'we got separated'
Decline the offer — you travel alone

dialogue.speaker: garcia
dialogue.text: Good. We leave at 5 AM. Priya handles weapons. Sam runs medical. You and your people handle fuel and watches.

dialogue.speaker: garcia
dialogue.text: I'm not a cruel man. I'm a careful one. There's a difference, and out here the difference keeps people breathing.

dialogue.speaker: priya
dialogue.text: About the kid. I've seen bites turn people in six hours. If he turns in the car, I'll put him down. That's not negotiable.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Danny is sitting outside, arm wrapped, pale. He doesn't know what they're saying about him. But he can guess.

dialogue.speaker: priya
dialogue.text: Kid asked me for water an hour ago. I gave it to him. If he turns, remember I did that too.

dialogue.speaker: garcia
dialogue.text: Your call. But that road north? It's not forgiving. If you get in trouble, don't come back here.

dialogue.speaker: garcia
dialogue.text: I've watched people drive off full of pride. None of them came back to gloat. Take the fuel. It's on the house.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You fill up the truck and drive north alone. The road is empty. The radio picks up static and fragments — coordinates, warnings, screaming.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Forty miles to Riverside. The road is blocked, detoured, and littered with the remains of people who tried to outrun the end.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Somewhere behind you, Garcia's group is either following or fortifying. Somewhere in your backseat, Danny is either sleeping or turning.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You'll know soon enough.

3.title: Chapter 3: Riverside
3.summary: The safe zone. The last stop. Every choice you've made walks through the gates with you — and not all of them are welcome.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Riverside. A walled community. Guard towers. Floodlights. People who look like they've been here long enough to feel safe — and suspicious of anyone who hasn't.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: A checkpoint. Medical screening. And a question on every wall, in every guard's eyes: who are you, and what did you do to get here?

dialogue.speaker: dr_chen
dialogue.text: I'm Dr. Chen. Medical screening. I need to check everyone in your vehicle for bites. This is non-negotiable.

dialogue.speaker: dr_chen
dialogue.text: I was an epidemiologist. I spent my whole career preparing for something like this. It didn't help. Maybe you'll be the exception.

dialogue.speaker: dr_chen
dialogue.text: If anyone is infected, we can offer them palliative care. We don't turn people away. But we do quarantine. Understand?

choices.text: Allow the screening — be honest about Danny
Allow the screening — you have nothing to hide
Refuse — you don't trust them

dialogue.speaker: dr_chen
dialogue.text: The bite is progressing. I'm sorry. He has maybe twelve hours before the fever takes him.

dialogue.speaker: dr_chen
dialogue.text: We can make him comfortable. And we have been working on something — experimental. No guarantees. It might slow the infection. It might not work at all.

dialogue.speaker: dr_chen
dialogue.text: I've watched forty-one people turn. I promised every one of them I'd try. I'm promising you the same thing now.

dialogue.speaker: danny
dialogue.text: I don't want to turn. Please. I don't want to be one of them.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Dr. Chen waits. Danny waits. The clock is the only thing that doesn't.

choices.text: Let Danny try the experimental treatment
Just make him comfortable — let him go peacefully
Spend his last hours with him

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The treatment is brutal. Danny screams. His fever spikes. Then, slowly, it breaks.

dialogue.speaker: dr_chen
dialogue.text: His vitals are stabilizing. I don't believe it. The infection is retreating.

dialogue.speaker: dr_chen
dialogue.text: Eleven trials. Eleven failures. I told myself after the last one that I was done experimenting on people. And then your friend walked in.

dialogue.speaker: danny
dialogue.text: Did it work? I feel... I feel okay. I actually feel okay.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You sit with Danny. He talks about his dad. About the dog. About a girl named Sofia he never got the nerve to talk to.

dialogue.speaker: danny
dialogue.text: You were the last good thing that happened to me. I want you to know that.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: At 3:47 AM — the same time everything started — Danny closes his eyes. He doesn't open them again.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You spend the last hours talking. About everything and nothing. He teaches you how to do a card trick. You teach him how to hotwire a car.

dialogue.speaker: danny
dialogue.text: If you find Sofia — her last name is Marchetti, she goes to Lincoln High — tell her I should have said something. That I was an idiot.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: He turns at dawn. Dr. Chen handles it. You don't watch. But you hear it.

dialogue.speaker: dr_chen
dialogue.text: Then you can't come in. I'm sorry. The rules exist for a reason.

dialogue.speaker: dr_chen
dialogue.text: I hope whatever you're hiding out there is worth the walls you won't enter. Good luck. Truly.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You sit in the truck outside the walls. Night falls. The sounds come closer.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: They come at midnight. A horde. Dozens. Maybe a hundred. Drawn by the lights of Riverside. The gates hold — for now.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You're outside the gates. The truck is running. You have seconds.

choices.text: Drive away — you don't owe these people anything
Fight alongside Riverside — sound the horn, draw the horde
Use the chaos to sneak inside the walls

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Riverside takes you in. It's not much — a cot, a meal, walls that hold. But it's more than most people have.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Weeks pass. You find a role. You find a rhythm. And then you find the radio message.

dialogue.speaker: radio
dialogue.text: [RADIO]: ...calling any survivors. Military convoy en route to Riverside. 48 hours. If you can hear this, hold on. Help is coming. Repeat...

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The horde comes before the convoy. Two thousand strong, drawn by something — sound, smell, or just the instinct to destroy what's alive.

dialogue.speaker: garcia
dialogue.text: We can hold the gate for an hour. Maybe two. If we evacuate through the north tunnel, we lose the settlement but we live.

dialogue.speaker: priya
dialogue.text: I counted the first wave. We don't have enough ammo to make a dent. Whatever we choose, choose it now.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: This is it. Everything you did — who you saved, who you abandoned, who you let in, who you left behind — it all comes down to this.

dialogue.speaker: garcia
dialogue.text: I've given orders in worse places. But never to people I actually care about. Make it count.

choices.text: Hold the gate — buy time for everyone to evacuate
Evacuate immediately — save who you can
Draw the horde away from Riverside — alone
Steal a vehicle and leave — let them sort it out
Tell Dr. Chen to release the experimental cure — risk it all
Keep your head down and stay silent — let the walls hold or fall without you

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You held the gate for three hours. When the convoy arrived, they found you slumped against the barricade, still breathing, still you.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Riverside survived because you bought them the time they needed. The convoy took you in. The bite on your arm healed. Nobody knows why.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Some people say it's because you did enough good to earn a second chance. Maybe. Or maybe the world just isn't done with you yet.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You evacuated 87 people through the north tunnel. Riverside fell, but the people didn't.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The convoy found you on the road two days later. A caravan of survivors and a story about someone who made the hard call at the right time.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You survived. You'll have to decide if that's enough.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You took the truck and drove south, horn blaring, radio screaming. The horde followed you. All of them.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Riverside never knew what you did. The convoy arrived to a settlement that was untouched. They found the truck three miles south, empty, doors open.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: They never found you. But Riverside lives. And that was the point.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You drove. The radio said the convoy was coming. You didn't turn back.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Weeks later, you hear that Riverside fell. Everyone. The convoy was too late. You don't know if that's your fault. You'll spend the rest of your life deciding.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The road goes on. So do you. Alone.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You slipped through the north gate during the chaos. Nobody saw you come in. Nobody cared.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Riverside fell that night. You survived by hiding in a storm drain while the screaming lasted six hours.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The convoy found you the next day. They asked what happened. You said you didn't know. They believed you. You wish you didn't.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Dr. Chen administered the experimental treatment to everyone — infected, exposed, everyone. The fever broke. The gray skin receded. The dead became... less dead.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: It wasn't a cure. Not really. But it was a chance. And in the first winter of the end, a chance was everything.

dialogue.speaker: dr_chen
dialogue.text: Forty-one people turned on my watch. This is for them. Every single one of them.

dialogue.speaker: dr_chen
dialogue.text: Danny was the key. His blood had something we'd never seen. If you hadn't brought him here... none of this would exist.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You saved the kid. The kid saved everyone. The dead hours are ending.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You made it through. Riverside took you in, eventually. You got a cot, a job, a routine.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: But you never told anyone about the voice at the door. The kid you left on the curb. The friend you let in when you shouldn't have.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The dead walk outside the walls. But some of the dead walk inside them too. The ones you carry.
